goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS feed content is imported with cook_method: raw_html bypassing all sanitization and rendered via raw post.cooked, allowing script injection/XSS from malicious feed entries

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly adds a `:raw_html` cook method that returns `raw` directly in `Post#cook` (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline where sanitization would typically occur. RSS/Atom content is imported in `Jobs::PollFeed` via `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The embed UI renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, so any HTML (including `<script>` or event-handler attributes) coming from a malicious feed entry would be output as-is into the iframe page, enabling XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of return false if not should_revise? causes revise! to always proceed even when content is unchanged, creating spurious revisions and risking overwrites of concurrent edits

adjudication.rationale: In lib/post_revisor.rb, the line `return false if not should_revise?` is still present after the change. The diff only removes a blank line following that guard (`-` empty line), not the guard itself. Therefore `revise!` will still short-circuit when `should_revise?` is false, and it will not always proceed or create spurious revisions based on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parent.postMessage uses request.referer as targetOrigin, which becomes empty string if referer is nil, meaning any origin per spec and leaking iframe content/metadata to any parent window

adjudication.rationale: In embed.html.erb the code does `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`, but the controller’s `ensure_embeddable` before_filter rejects requests with a missing referer (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), so `request.referer` should not be nil/blank on any successful render. Also, an empty-string `targetOrigin` does not mean “any origin” (that would be `"*"`). While using the full referer URL (including path) as `targetOrigin` may be incorrect/exception-prone, the specific claimed leak via nil->empty-string wildcard is not a verifiable issue in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: if post.present? should be if post.persisted?; present? returns true for unsaved posts with validation or database errors, causing TopicEmbed records pointing to non-existent posts

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `post = creator.create` and then `if post.present?` creates a `TopicEmbed` with `topic_id: post.topic_id` and `post_id: post.id`. Even if `post.present?` were true for an unsaved/invalid `Post` object, `post.id` (and likely `post.topic_id`) would be `nil` for a non-persisted record, and the migration defines `topic_id`/`post_id` as `null: false` plus a `create!`, so the `TopicEmbed` row would not be created (it would raise and the transaction would roll back). Therefore the specific claimed outcome—creating `TopicEmbed` records pointing to non-existent posts—is not a verifiable issue in this diff; at worst it would raise an exception rather than silently create bad references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding force: true to create_table :top_topics drops and recreates the table, destroying existing top_topics data on re-run or in parallel migration environments

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` would drop an existing `top_topics` table if present, this migration (versioned `20131223171005`) will not be re-run on databases that have already applied it (it’s recorded in `schema_migrations`). On fresh installs the table doesn’t exist yet, so no data is dropped. On rollback/re-migrate, the table would be dropped/recreated regardless, so `force: true` doesn’t introduce additional data loss in normal migration workflows. The finding hinges on atypical scenarios (concurrent migration runs or a pre-existing table without the migration being marked applied), which isn’t a clear, verifiable defect from the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition between where(embed_url: url).first and TopicEmbed.create! allows concurrent requests for the same URL to attempt duplicate topic creation, causing unhandled unique constraint violations

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a post/topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so two concurrent calls for the same `url` can both observe no existing row and then race on `create!`, causing one to raise an unhandled uniqueness violation (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`). There is no locking or rescue around the check-then-insert sequence, so the race is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls doesn't handle protocol-relative URLs (e.g. //cdn.example.com/img.png); they start with / and are incorrectly rewritten to http://embeddable_host/cdn.example.com/img.png

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and img URL rewriting use `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` (same for `src`) and then set `a['href'] = "#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. A protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` starts with `/`, so it will be rewritten to something like `http://<original-host>/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is incorrect and changes the resource host. This behavior is directly implied by the code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If the RetrieveTopic job fails or embed_url is invalid, the loading page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no error state or max-retry limit

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil it always enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... ) and renders 'loading'. The loading template (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) unconditionally does document.location.reload() every 30 seconds with no attempt counter or error handling. If the RetrieveTopic job never creates a TopicEmbed (e.g., embed_url is not a valid URI so TopicRetriever#invalid_host? returns true and retrieval is skipped, or the fetch/import fails), subsequent requests will continue to render the loading page and auto-reload indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed category option in Disqus thor task breaks existing functionality; imported Disqus threads can no longer be assigned to a specific category

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `:category` Thor option was removed, along with the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)`. The new implementation imports via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` create the post via `PostCreator.new(...)` without any category parameter. Therefore, Disqus imports can no longer be assigned to a specific category via the task, which is a concrete loss of prior functionality introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses Kernel#open which can execute shell commands if the URL starts with |; should use URI.open or a dedicated HTTP client

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. With open-uri loaded, `open` is the Kernel method that still supports the "pipe" form (e.g., a string starting with `|`), which can spawn a shell command. Since the value comes from a setting and is not validated/parsed as a URI before calling `open`, this is a concrete command-execution footgun in the added code (even if the setting is typically admin-controlled). Using `URI.open` (or an HTTP client) would avoid the pipe behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) accepts empty-string origin since indexOf("") === 0, allowing messages from sandboxed or data-URI iframes with empty origin to pass the security check

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler checks `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. It is true in JavaScript that `"...".indexOf("") === 0`, so if `e.origin` were the empty string the check would pass. However, for sandboxed/data-URI/opaque origins, browsers provide the literal string origin value "null" (or another non-empty string), not an empty string; with "null" this check would return -1 and correctly reject. The proposed finding hinges specifically on an empty-string origin, which is not a verifiable/standard behavior from the diff alone, so it’s not a solid, real issue as stated (though the substring-based origin check is generally weak for other reasons not claimed here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Port omission logic (uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443) is scheme-agnostic, incorrectly omitting the port for non-standard combinations like http://host:443/ or https://host:80/

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix is built as `scheme://host` and then appends `:port` only if `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This check is scheme-agnostic, so it will incorrectly omit an explicitly non-default port when the scheme/port combination is unusual (e.g., `http://example.com:443/...` yields no `:443` in `prefix`, and `https://example.com:80/...` yields no `:80`). That would generate wrong absolute URLs for relative `href`/`src` when importing content from such URLs.
